Why I Think This World Should End

Ted Cruz tried to insult Donald Trump the other night during the so-called "debates" by referring to him as a New Yorker with New York attitude.

Regardless of what one thinks about New York City and New Yorkers in general, the Big Apple is a tough town and indeed not a place for the faint of heart. But it is also a city filled with all kinds of people with plenty of grit and compassion. Trump is one of them.

People who spend time with Trump typically come away really liking him. To that end, here are a few anecdotes I'd like to share.

Back in the 80s around the time Trump published his book "The Art of the Deal," my girlfriend had accumulated quite a bit of debt after four years of college. She was eager to find work upon graduation but did not have a car to take her to interviews so she decided to write Trump and ask him to give her one. She pledged to never forget his act of kindness and generosity and would reciprocate after she became successful in her chosen profession.

Several weeks later, she received a gold embossed letter from one of his secretaries with the Trump organization. In it she explained that Mr. Trump received frequent requests from people like my girlfriend but that he had already made numerous commitments to a variety of charitable organizations that year, leaving open the possibility that she could try again another time. Neither one of us had really expected that Trump would ever give her a new car but we were surprised and impressed that he actually had someone respond so respectfully to what we knew was a preposterous request.

Many people who have followed Trump's career are aware of his love for the game of golf and how this love has lead him to build courses all over the world including NYC and Scotland. A few years ago he was invited to speak at the United States Golf Association in New Jersey where he talked about his experiences as a businessman and avid golfer.

According to my friends who were in attendance, Trump spoke thoughtfully, politely and believe it or don't, modestly. None of the brash, braggadocio that most people think about when they think about Trump was on display at the event and he didn't leave until everyone who wanted to shake his hand or get his autograph got one. My friends said he was remarkably low-key, respectful and charming.

As one of the world's most famous landlords, it wouldn't be surprising to me that Trump might be a bit grouchy if kids hit a ball into his yard or cut across his front lawn to get someplace fast. But not the Donald.

Trump owns a few buildings in Manhattan and about ten years ago my friends and I decided to skateboard through the lobbies of each of them. We did it to see if we could get away with it and because we wanted to have a story to tell.

Yeah, we were being obnoxious. We could have been arrested for trespassing. But nothing of the kind occurred. Trump personnel saw us skating through on the polished marble floors, doing jumps and back scratchers, but appeared too busy to say or do anything. Of course, we were nervous and didn't want to stick around long enough to be caught so we high tailed it out of there. Funniest thing about the experience though was how the doorman in each building opened up the doors for us as we skated on through to the sidewalk.

For all his brashness and bravado, Donald Trump is actually a pretty nice guy. For a New Yawker.
